_: Ride-along and doorstep lines, merged by story.js applyDialogue (the file replaces the fallback per who+when). Canon: docs/STORY-LEDGER.md, docs/STORY-REBUILD.md. Margaret is Tom's mother and never rides with the gang: her start/end here are Tom leaving and coming home, spoken from her driveway (avatars.js margaretLine). Tom's father did not live at 299 Fraser and has no pool here; he is only a phone call (story.js DAD_CALLS). Language (Tom, 6 Oct and 20 Oct 2026): the main cast speaks English; Sayyad's pools rewritten English-first on 20 Oct (S1-ENGLISH). Adam's pool still waits for the second sitting.

dialogue.line: Two minutes. I'm up. I'm up. OK, go.
OK so listen: the new PowerBook keyboard lights up. Lights up.
Say hi to your mom for me. She likes me, I think.
The iPod holds a thousand songs. Mike put two hundred. Two hundred.
I have a theory about your alternator. Listen. No, listen.
Sorry, sorry. I slept. I really slept.
Theory: if we take Lucerne, we save four minutes.
Turn the radio down, there are ladies on the sidewalk.
My Mac crashed once this year. Once. That's a record.
Seatbelt. No, you. And me too.
Let's go. I planned everything. Roughly.
I read your owner's manual. There's a fuse for everything.
Okay. That was a ride.
Thanks, man. Seriously. Thanks.
Clean job, my man.
Drop me on Denise-Friend. My mom's ferns need water. Don't ask.
I'm going back to bed. That's not a joke.
Next time, call first. I won't answer, but call.
Mission accomplished. Double cheeseburger for my moral support.
Perfect timing. I can still get on MSN before supper.
Tell your mom thanks for the pasta. From last week.
My theory: you braked too early. But it's fine.
Nice. If you need an elite copilot tomorrow, call the house.
Wait, I left my Discman in your truck. Keep it warm.
Where are you off to? ...I'm just asking.
Take a sweater. It gets cold by the river.
Is Abraham going? ...Okay. Say hello to Abraham.
Call if you're going to be late. Call before.
Gas in it? Of course. You pay for it.
Seatbelt. I'm watching from the window, Tom.
Who's in the truck with you? I'm just asking.
Don't let Sayyad talk you into anything. He's too polite.
Drive like I'm in the truck.
If Mike asks, the couch is not coming here.
There's gas money in the jar. ...Don't take all of it.
Have fun. Not too much fun.
You're home. Good. What did you break?
Did you eat? Sit. There's pasta.
You were quick. Too quick. Where did you go?
Your friends can come in. Shoes off.
Mike's mother called. About a couch. I said nothing.
Is that a new scratch? Don't tell me.
You smell like a gas station, Tom.
Sayyad said hello to me. Very polite boy. What does he want?
You're in one piece. The truck too? Good.
Your father called. He sounded happy. Call him back.
The basement light was on all day. Just saying.
Home before dark. I'm impressed. Suspicious, but impressed.
Mon Sunfire a encore pété son alternateur hier. Fait qu'on prend ton truck.
Pèse su'l gaz. Plus vite c'est fini, plus vite j'peux aller rien faire chez nous.
Touche pas au poste de radio. Le silence me dérange moins que tes goûts musicaux.
Si la transmission lâche, j'pousse pas. J'ai mal au dos.
Y fait trente degrés, ton air climatisé pousse du vent tiède. Formidable.
Le chemin Pink est plein de trous. Essaie d'en éviter au moins un sur deux.
Si quelqu'un demande, j'suis à Mayo. J'suis toujours à Mayo.
On part. Essaie de pas faire caler le moteur aux lumières comme la semaine passée.
J'ai un sac de chips sel et vinaigre sous le banc. Mange-les pas, c'est mon dîner.
Si on se fait pogner par les flics, c'est toé qui as le volant, j'te connais pas.
Encore une ride d'Aylmer... La ville où y se passe jamais rien à part la rouille qui pousse.
Envoye, décolle. J'ai deux heures à perdre avant de retourner à Mayo.
C'est fini. Mon dos a survécu à ta suspension en bois d'arbre.
On est vivants. C'est déjà plus que ce à quoi je m'attendais en partant.
Parke ça croche de même, de toute façon personne vient jamais dans ce coin-là.
Bon. J'm'en va m'coucher devant Télétoon en buvant du Tang.
T'as manqué le poteau d'un pied. Beau travail d'improvisation.
J'ai plus de sensation dans ma jambe droite, mais la livraison est faite.
Débarque-moé là. Le soleil me tape su'a tête pis ton banc sent le chien mouillé.
Au moins le moteur a pas explosé. Pas encore.
Voilà. Une autre journée passionnante qui s'achève dans le grand Aylmer.
J'ai laissé un emballage de Jos Louis dans ta porte. Tu remercieras la visite.
On a fini. Whatever. M'a aller voir si mon Sunfire veut démarrer.
Pas pire. On a évité la police pis la scrap pour aujourd'hui.
